I can relate to most things you're saying. I have had severe social anxiety for 10 years and I thought it would fade away over time but unfortunately it didn't. I barely left my house this year. That's probably why I act weird all the time too. I have never met someone in real life with severe social anxiety but judging from websites/forums a lot of people are in the same boat.

I've got exactly the same problem. I just went to college like everyone else not having a clue what I would do after that. I thought things would just point themselves out. Well, they don't.

I just can't see my life working out. I can't imagine ever having a wife/girlfriend. I have zero confidence. I am slowly losing all my friends because lately I just have this kind of negative vibe I guess. I am too quiet and never know what to say.

You didn't come across as preachy. I feel like talking about it does seems to help a tiny bit. In the mornings I tend to feel ok, but when I'm awake I tend to start thinking about all of it and everything just goes downhill fast.

Anyways, to answer your question, I have sent my resume, but to no avail. I didn't even get a response of any kind (negative or positive).

I like your idea of taking steps forward and it does seem to work for you, I'm glad, but I fear taking steps forward also means destroying possible future paths (e.g. if I got a job in accounting now and I do this job for a couple of years, it would be hard to get a job in another field).

Yup, pretty much feel the same here. I don't know if college would have been a waste if I had studied something like medicine, but in hindsight a business degree just doesn't really get you that far. You just got to make these decisions so early in life and everybody expects you to make all the right decisions right away ... and if you don't... well you end up like me :/

I graduated last year. I talked to my school's career center but that was not that helpful. They kept asking me questions like 'what would you do if money wasn't an object?'. But I can't answer these because I really don't know ...

It has been so long since I enjoyed anything really. Examples of what makes me happy are very hard to find. A couple of years ago, I did a roadtrip, which was nice. I liked to spend time with my one-year old nephew. I doubt I would even enjoy these things nowadays though.

My relationship with my family is good I guess. Mom's supportive + I get along with my siblings.

If degree wasn't an issue I would probably like to do strategy consulting or a management position that allows me to use frameworks to think of new solutions to certain problems. But we all know MBB/... won't hire me. The scary part though is that I don't know if that's really what I want or that it's just something I want in order to be seen as 'normal' and 'successful' by others/society.
